Mark Plays Nuitai

A blind playtest of the pygame demo by Mark, an invented professional playtester, thinking out loud. His notes follow the episode.

Mark Hey everyone, welcome back. Episode 4. Quick recap of where we are: last time the bridge troll, the Nuno sa Tulay, flattened us, the game threw me back to my Episode 1 save, and I spent the rest of the session rebuilding. I'm standing right outside the Crossroads Inn with 330 pule, saved at the grove totem.

Mark Today I want three things. Water that third post for Lanu, the one in Maika's glade, which means figuring out how you actually carry water in this game. Find the Sage again, because I couldn't last time. And if I'm feeling brave and well stocked, go back to that troll with a real plan and a fresh save.

Mark First thing, and I should've tried this last episode. There's a lake right here, east of the Crossroads. The booklet said you scoop water by facing it and pressing A. I don't own a cup that I know of. Let's just see what the game says.

Mark "Just foam and sand." So that's salt water, or at least not the kind the game wants. Fair enough.

Mark While I'm in the menu, let me finally answer two old questions. Shoulder buttons flip the bag pages, not left and right. Seer's Shell: "Scans one enemy in a fight." There it is. I've been carrying two of those for three episodes. And the Frying Pan says "Raises Strength but lowers Vitality. Found along the way, not made to order." I like that last bit, it implies gear can be made to order somewhere.

Mark Key Items is just the Leaf Pouch. No cup. And look, each of us has a bag count, Kailo "Bag 3/4", Hina "Bag 1/4". After last episode's Life Totem fiasco I want to move a healer into Hina's bag before any boss.

Mark The quest page: "The Lanu sage asked you to water the five posts in the grove. Water each one, then go back and tell the sage." Two of five. If I had to guess, the Sage hands you a cup, and I used them up on the first two. That "lanu_cups" thing I half remember from the Sage. So, up to the grove.

Mark Grove villagers. The knees guy again, and two lines I hadn't heard. "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning. It is hers anyway, but she likes being asked." And "Shh. If you hold still, you can hear the rain coming before it comes." Nice. The first one is a clue, I think. Water from a spring, not from these healing ponds.

Mark No Sage, again. He's just not standing in the grove anymore. That's two sessions running I can't find the guy who gave me the quest.

Mark Area map. Okay, look at the bottom left. That maze south of the west screen has blue in its corner. That's the screen with the four chests. Real water, maybe a stream. And the screen west of the Crossroads has a gap at its top I've never taken. If I had to guess where the Maki Sages walked off to, it's up there.

Mark Mushroom on the way in, the 'Ōkole 'Iole, and it got a preemptive on us. Or we got one on it, "Preemptive strike!", the turn bar was all us. Kailo's Mediums are doing 20 to 23, and Hina's are doing 14, 15. That's way up from the 2 to 4 she was doing in Episode 1. Stats rising by use, I guess that's what it looks like over three sessions.

Mark It tried to put Kailo to sleep, "Kailo couldn't fall asleep." Ha. Then it fell. Ti Leaf.

Mark Then a boar. Oh, here's something I never noticed. When I move the cursor between Attack, Cook and Element, the turn bar on the right reshuffles. It's previewing how each choice changes the order. That's the Final Fantasy X turn list, and it's exactly what this chain system needed.

Mark Sauté on a sleeping boar in nature stance. "Weak!", 24, and "Burn". One mark of mana. Then I parried all three blows of its string, two Strongs and a Light, and Kailo countered for 28. And the burn finished it. "Wild Boar is burning and cannot be healed." Boar Hide number six.

Mark Oh, new screen. The gap at the top of the west maze. And there's a fourth post, right here by a pond. And a lot of company. Four Papanoks, two mushrooms, and two boars parked right in front of the north exit like bouncers.

Mark Post first. The narrator calls it "a carved post with a cup of water", which, I think that's just how it's drawn, there's a little blue bowl at its foot. Kailo: "A post for Lanu. I need a cup of water to leave her an offering." Same line as the glade post. The pond next to it: "The party drinks from the cool pond. Everyone is rested." Healing, not scooping.

Mark So now I know where four of the five posts are and I can water none of them. I'm going to look at that north exit, then go ask around about cups.

Mark Two Papanoks on the way across. Their seven-Light string is the rhythm one, and I'm getting it every time now, "Parried!" seven in a row, and Kailo's counter hit for 38. When it lands clean like that it really does feel like a drum line. The second one dropped an element, "Haste". The rooster's own speed-up spell. I'll give that to someone in a minute.

Mark Mushroom ambush on the walk up. And here, both bars full, Kailo and Hina next to each other on the turn bar, and Combo lights up on the right page. Pōhuehue again.

Mark All five notes, then the spin, cracked at the top. 238.

Mark Whoa. That's one shot on a monster that heals 80 a turn. I still think this is the best thing in the game. What I like is that you build toward it. Every Light and every parry earlier in the fight was filling those bars, so the big moment is something you earned rather than something you picked from a list. Red Cap.

Mark Two more Papanoks, a pair this time. One of them shifted to light stance and hit Hina for 48, "Weak!" That's the flower side taking light, I think. No meter on that one, again, the elemental hits just land. Both fell to counters off clean parries. Red Feather and a Kukui. And my max HP went up mid-fight, 130 to 140, "Kailo's Vitality up!" Getting hit is how you get tougher. I like that it happens right there in the fight instead of on a level-up screen.

Mark Hina's Heal is still 18. For one mark, sure, but at 170 max that's a Band-Aid.

Mark Now, the north exit. I walked the whole corridor under that wall of palms pushing up at every single column. Solid, all twelve. So it's the grove door trick again. The boars are standing in a pocket you reach from the other side. I'll find the other side some day.

Mark Tried to give Haste out. "Turns come sooner." Kailo: "KAILO can't learn this." And Hina's box is greyed, so her neither. Huh. So elements are tied to who can use them, and this one belongs to nobody I have. If I had to guess, Haste is a wind or air thing, and there's a third party member out there whose stance it fits. Which would fit Melia, actually. Or whoever the Kagura Fan was for.

Mark A boar jumped us on the way back. It shifted to fire and hit Hina "Weak!" for 14, no meter, same as always. And when it fell, another element. "Flambé." Kailo's fire again, I'd bet. Sauté's big brother.

Mark Back at the Crossroads. Let's go ask the innkeeper about cups. Every road runs past her door, she said. Somebody here sells dishes.

Mark Small correction to myself, I called the innkeeper "her" a minute ago. The game hasn't said. Just "Innkeeper".

Mark Inn round. The cook has a menu now, "How does the pot choose a dish?", "What is salt for?", "What if it makes ???". Same pot rules I wrote down before. Then "Then stand back. Something is about to boil over." The innkeeper's same as ever, and the shop has nothing like a cup. The Traveler: "Eat before you fight. That is all I know."

Mark And there's a Boy by the produce baskets I never talked to. "Seaweed washes up on the beach. Fish bite if you have a rod and patience." Okay, so the stew's four Fish means a fishing rod. Writing that down. "Pork comes from boars. I don't go near boars." And when you say never mind: "Okay. Do you want to see my crab?" I do, kid. I really do.

Mark Here's where I am though. That's two episodes I've been walking past Lanu's posts with no cup. The lake, the grove, the grove's pond, the inn, its shop, everybody in it. I'm calling this one stuck. I'm opening the booklet for one word, "cup", and closing it.

Mark Okay. "Cup" isn't in it at all. So I tried "water" and found the bit I half remembered from last time, under "Fresh Water": "Face a river or a pond and press A to scoop up fresh water for cooking. Seawater is no good, and neither is the shore. A spring with little sparkles over it heals instead of giving water." And it mentions "the canteens". I'll admit my eye caught the fishing paragraph right next to it, something about an Old Rod. I'm closing it.

Mark So that's the whole confusion. Every pond I've tried at a post has sparkles, and sparkles mean a healing spring. The post wants plain water, and the game calls a cup of plain water "a cup of water" without ever saying "you need to scoop it from a river first." The grove villager said it, "water from the spring", and the booklet says springs don't give water. Those two disagree a little, by the way.

Mark Where's plain water? The map showed blue at the bottom left of the southwest maze, and the pond screen north of the village had a river, I think. Southwest is closer.

Mark Got through the west maze again, with a boar and a mushroom on the way. The mushroom dropped a Seer's Shell. And here's the four-chest screen.

Mark And there's the water, bottom left. But I'm in the little top pocket again, the one with the chest I already opened, and every row below me is a wall of palms. The water's walled off from this side.

Mark Oh, wait. Look at the area map now. There are two blues. The lake by the Crossroads and the sea strip along the east are a dark teal. The water here, and a river across the pond screen north of the village, are a light sky blue. That's the code, isn't it. Teal is salt, light blue is fresh. Nobody told me that, but it's consistent, and it's a nice quiet way to teach it if it's on purpose.

Mark And now the map shows the pond screen too, bottom left, with a river right across the top of it. I watered that post in Episode 1, so I must have scooped there without knowing what I was doing. That's my water. It's the long way round, but I know the road. Crossroads, south through the mazes, the village, then north.

Mark Back through the west maze the way I came, and an Aghoy pair jumps us on the Crossroads road. Blue first, since that's the one that drains. Focused it down in two turns, then the Green. 'Awa Tonic, Blue Wing, another Seer's Shell, and 90 pule. 420 now.

Mark Two more Blue Aghoys in the maze south of the Crossroads, one at a time this time, which is fine. One dropped a "Niu Putong". Kailo's wearing a "Honu Putong" already, so that's a relic. Honu's a turtle. Niu, coconut, I think. And an 'Ōlena, turmeric.

Mark Now, the next maze down, the one with all the boars, has a west exit I've never taken. On the area map there's a blank square right there, between the four-chest screen and the pond screen. If I had to guess, that blank square is the missing link, and the pond screen's "unreachable" north exit comes out in it. Worth a look on the way.

Mark Oh, hello. The west exit doesn't go to the pond screen. It opens on a big two-story hale with produce crates out front, a little river in the corner, and a sign: "Hunters' Lodge". That's the place the Boar Hide's been telling me about since Episode 1.

Mark The Trapper. "No kapa for sale. Monsters carry it. Bark cloth, beaten thin. Each one has a move drawn on it, step by step. Got a spare? I'll buy it." So kapa are move scrolls. Then "E komo mai! What'll it be?", and one of the options is "Hunts".

Mark A hunt board. "Great Boar, Nuno sa Tulay, Six Aghoy, Walking Corpse." Walking Corpse, okay, that's new and I don't love it. The Great Boar "Pays 800 pule." Taking it, Kailo's already going after that pig for free. And the Nuno: "That Nuno at the river bend takes a toll off everyone who crosses. Put him down and I'll pay 600 pule." Yes. Kailo paid that troll a hundred pule and then got flattened by him. He'd want this one personally.

Mark Sold all six Boar Hides, 50 each. 810 pule. The gear's all trade-offs, every piece. "Spear. Strength up, Intelligence down." "Fan. Willpower up, Vitality down." The Ananá set: "Fire resist, nature weak." "Pearl Anklet": "Shadow resist, spirit weak." I like that a lot. There's no strictly better item, so buying is a decision about what you're about to fight. The catch is nothing here covers spirit, which is what the troll hit me with. And there's a "Bag Upgrade", "The next size up, for one member", a Coir Belt for 300.

Mark And then a whole scene. A white-haired woman, Miki. "You there. Have you seen a man with white hair and a mouth that never stops? Tall. Looks like he's doing you a favor by existing." Kailo: "...Maybe? Who's asking?" "His sister. He walked out of Māla Iki without a word, and our mother has been asking where he is ever since. He's a flake. I came all this way to drag him home."

Mark Then she spots Hina. "Oh look, Māla priestess. I thought I'd left your kind behind on Māla Iki." Hina: "Funny. I was thinking the same about yours." Ha. Then Kailo, who only has one thing on his mind: "Is that shoyu? I need some for Pono's stew." She won't share, so he makes a deal. Find the brother, get the bottle. And to Hina: "It's what makes the braise dark and salty. Without it, it's eggs floating in coconut. Not for Pono."

Mark Okay, sorting this out. Miki, the brother's sister, holds the Māla Shoyu from my stew list. Her brother has white hair and a big mouth and left home without a word. But here's what's bugging me. The Loremaster told me this island is Māla Iki. And Miki says her brother "walked out of Māla Iki" and she thought she'd left the Māla priests behind "on Māla Iki". So either she's saying they both came from here and she just got back, or there's a mix-up in the writing. If I had to guess, Miki's from Kota Emas or somewhere Hina's from too, given that little exchange. Writing it down as a question.

Mark Other hunters. "A Seer's Shell tells you what a beast is made of, and how much fight it has left." Should've been using those. "Everyone who fights carries three kinds of weapon, and each kind has its own Skill. Whatever weapon you hold decides which Skill you can use." So that's the Weapon command on the left page. And this one I like: "A tree was in my way out there. Too thick to get around. I wished I had an axe." That's the palm walls. That's a tool for the Y button, I'd bet anything.

Mark Wait, the little figure on the table talks. Very slowly. "Ahh... a... visitor..." "I am... Gaju... maru..." "Do you... know... Kaigara...?" Kailo: "Kai-what?" "Shells... and... patience..." "Sit... I will... teach you..."

Mark So a board game, played with shells. I asked where it's from. "Kami Kuku... the Kame Kingdom..." "Far... to the northwest... green islands... clear springs..." "Great turtles... swim there... older than... anyone..." "We heal... the sick... with what... the springs give..."

Mark Okay, I love this. Gajumaru is the Okinawan banyan tree, the one the little tree spirits live in, and kaigara is Japanese for seashell, and Kame is turtle. So the Kame Kingdom is the Ryukyu Kingdom, Okinawa, off to the northwest. So now there's a Philippine folklore family, the Malay in Hina's mouth, Kota Emas, and an Okinawa. The map of this world is the Pacific, all of it. I'm not playing his game right now because I'm chasing water, but he says "I will... be... right... here..." and I believe him.

Mark South of the lodge, and it is the pond screen, the river right across the top. Facing the water, A.

Mark "Kailo scoops up some fresh water." Finally. Two whole episodes. And again, and again, five times, until "Oof. These canteens are getting heavy." Ha. So he had canteens the whole time, they're just not an item you see.

Mark Here's my honest read on this. The fix the game needs is tiny. The post's line could say "I need fresh water from a river" instead of "a cup of water", and I'd have been done in Episode 2. "Cup" made me hunt for an object. The light-blue map color is a lovely touch, but you only learn it by already knowing the answer.

Mark Now, posts. The one north of the west maze is the one I know the road to. Back through the lodge screen and the boar maze.

Mark Back up through the boar maze, the Crossroads, the west maze, to the post with the pond. And now Kailo says something different. "A post for Lanu. I'll leave her a cup of water as an offering." "Offer Lanu a cup of water?" Yes. "Kailo poured Lanu a cup of water."

Mark That's three of five. And a Papanok jumped us the second the cup was down, which, sure. Seven parries, done in two turns. Red Feather.

Mark Next the glade post, east of the grove. And the grove has the totem, so I'll save on the way. It's been since Episode 3 and I'm carrying two episodes' worth of progress again.

Mark Grove totem. "The party kneels at the totem and tells the Akua all that has happened." Saved over slot 1. "The Pork Strikes Back" still, 1:08 on the save clock, 810 pule. That feels good. Everything from this session is safe now: the money, the hunts, the water, the third post.

Mark Out the grove's east door, and it drops me in the little nook again, the one with the chest I opened in Episode 1. Two mushrooms in here this time, one with a "!" over it. Two fights, Ti Leaf and a Red Cap.

Mark And from here I can see the glade post, top left, by its sparkly pond, and Maika's sand patch with the sign, and a ring of four boars over on the right I don't remember. But I'm in the nook. I pushed right against that column of palms on both bottom rows. Solid. So this door really is a one-way drop into a pocket, and the only way back out is the door I came in. The glade post is reached from the south, the long loop over the bridge and the beach.

Mark That's the thing about these palm mazes that's starting to wear on me. Twice today a screen showed me what I wanted, the north exit with the boars and now this post, and both times the screen I was standing in was a sealed room. Once is a nice reveal. Every time, it reads like the map's teasing me. The hunter's axe line makes me think there's a tool coming that fixes this, and if so, I'd love the game to say "you'll be able to clear these later" somewhere.

Mark Quick menu stop. Flambé to Kailo: "KAILO learned Flambé!" But his grid only has the one row right now, Sauté and Wave Guard, and Sauté reads "Hits one enemy with fire. 12 physical fire, 20% burn." So Flambé waits on the bench until he earns a second row. Fine. I like that the description gives actual numbers here, it's the first time I've seen the game show its math.

Mark Back in the grove. I walked up the east side to the top rows behind the pond, the one part of this screen I'd never stood in, looking for the Sage. Nobody. Just palms. So the man who gave me the quest has been gone since Episode 1, and the quest says "go back and tell the sage". I don't know where back is. If I had to guess, he walked off into the Lost Woods with the other Maki Sages, and the fifth post is out there too.

Mark Quest page. Six open now: "Stew for the wake", "MIKI's brother", "Soy sauce", "Lanu's five posts", "Hunt: the Great Boar", "Hunt: the toll Nuno". Posts, three of five.

Mark But look at Miki's page. "Miki wants to know where her brother is. You know now, so go to the hunters' lodge and tell her." I know now? I don't. Kailo said "...Maybe?" when she described him, so the game thinks Kailo has met a tall white-haired guy with a big mouth. I haven't. Unless... the only person I've been told about and never found is the Sage. No, the Sage was Lanu's man, he wouldn't have walked out of anywhere. If I had to guess, it's someone I met in Episode 1 I'm not remembering, or the quest skipped a step. Either way, let's go test it. Saved again first, 1:11 on the clock.

Mark Two screens of mazes later, an Aghoy fight on the way, Green Wing. And Miki, when I talk to her: "Find my brother and tell me where he is. The bottle is yours." So she doesn't think I know either. The quest page jumped ahead of the story. I'll flag that one for the studio.

Mark While I was here, I sat back down with Gajumaru and asked how he got here. "A Bandari... trader... from Kota Emas..." "My friend... Gin'imun... and I... rode with him..." "His ship... was fast... too fast..." "He sold... his goods... and left... without us..." "Gin'imun... swam on... to Māla Iki..." Kailo: "Your friend just left you here?" And Gajumaru: "I was... still... thinking... about my move..."

Mark Ha. That's the best line in the episode. He missed his boat because he was mid-game. And it's the second time today someone's said Māla Iki like it's somewhere else. His friend "swam on to Māla Iki", so this island is not Māla Iki. I wrote down three episodes ago that the island was Māla Iki. I think I had that wrong, and Māla Iki is the next island over, the one Miki's brother walked out of and Hina's priests run. Which makes the Loremaster's line make more sense too, if I misheard which island he meant.

Mark And Kaigara: "Black shells... white shells... a chalk grid..." "Surround... the other's shells... and they are... yours..." "Black... always... goes first..." "Some games... last... years..." "This one... started... last spring..." That's Go. A Go-playing tree spirit who's been mid-game since spring. I'm going to play him next time, I promise.

Mark One more for the hunt board. "They say a dead man walks at night. If you find him, lay him down and I'll pay 1200 pule." The Walking Corpse. I said Not now. Kailo's got a wake to cook for tonight, and a dead man walking around on the night of Old Pono's wake is not something he'd take money for before he knew who it was. If I had to guess, and I really hope I'm wrong, it's Pono. The Callers of Makua "talk to the dead". Somebody may have talked a little too loud.

Mark And that's a good place to stop. We're standing outside the Hunters' Lodge with 855 pule, the game saved at the grove at 1:11, with only the last Aghoy fight and a couple of conversations since. Three of Lanu's five posts are watered, I finally know how water works, and I've got a bounty on the troll who beat me. Next time I want to water the glade post the long way round, find whoever the fifth post and the Sage are hiding behind, get Kailo a fishing rod for those four Fish, and then go back to that bridge and collect my 600 pule from the Nuno. Thanks for hanging out, everyone. See you next time.

End of episode

What happened

1. Started on the map at the Crossroads beside the Inn (330 pule). Faced the lake east of the Crossroads and pressed A: "Just foam and sand." Checked the bag pages (L/R flip them): no cup; Seer's Shell "Scans one enemy in a fight."; quest page Lanu's five posts 2 / 5.

2. Lanu's Grove: talked to three villagers (knees line; "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning..."; "Shh. If you hold still..."). No Sage. Area map.

3. West of the Crossroads: fought an 'Ōkole 'Iole (preemptive strike; dropped Ti Leaf) and a Wild Boar (Sauté burn, three parries, counter; Boar Hide).

4. North of the west maze (new screen): found the fourth Lanu post by a sparkling pond ("I need a cup of water"); the pond only heals. Fought Papanok (Kukui Nut), Papanok (element Haste), 'Ōkole 'Iole (Pōhuehue combo for 238; Red Cap), Papanok pair (Kukui, Red Feather). Tested every column of the palm row under the north exit: all solid. Tried to give Haste: "KAILO can't learn this." Hina greyed.

5. Back through the west maze: Wild Boar (Flambé element). Crossroads Inn: Cook's menu, Innkeeper, Traveler, Boy ("Fish bite if you have a rod and patience."; crab).

6. Opened the booklet once (see The booklet). West maze again (Wild Boar: Ti Leaf; 'Ōkole 'Iole: Red Cap, Seer's Shell) to the four-chest screen: the water is walled off from the top pocket. Area map shows light blue (fresh) versus teal (salt).

7. Crossroads road: Green Aghoy + Blue Aghoy ('Awa Tonic, Blue Wing, Seer's Shell, 90 pule). Maze south of the Crossroads: Blue Aghoy (Blue Wing, Niu Putong), Blue Aghoy ('Ōlena).

8. Boar maze's west exit: new screen with the Hunters' Lodge. Trapper: kapa line, shop, Hunts board. Took "Hunt: the Great Boar" (800 pule) and the Nuno sa Tulay hunt (600 pule). Sold 6 Boar Hide for 300 (810 pule). Bought nothing. Met Miki (new quests "MIKI's brother" and "Soy sauce"). Hunters' tips (Seer's Shell, three weapon kinds, axe). Met Gajumaru (Kaigara board game; from the Kame Kingdom).

9. South of the lodge screen is the pond screen: scooped fresh water five times ("Oof. These canteens are getting heavy.").

10. Walked back north (lodge screen, boar maze, maze, Crossroads, west maze) to the fourth post: "Offer Lanu a cup of water?" Yes. Posts 3 / 5. Papanok fight right after (Red Feather).

11. Lanu's Grove: saved slot 1 (1:08, 810 pule). Took the east door: sealed nook with two 'Ōkole 'Iole (Ti Leaf, Red Cap); the glade post visible but unreachable from the nook. Gave Flambé to Kailo ("KAILO learned Flambé!"), no free slot. Searched the top of the grove for the Sage: nobody. Quest page: six open. Saved again (1:11, 810 pule).

12. Back to the Hunters' Lodge (Green Aghoy on the way: Green Wing). Miki: "Find my brother and tell me where he is." Gajumaru: how he got here, what Kaigara is. Trapper's Walking Corpse hunt (1200 pule): Not now.

13. Ended at about 58:30 on the episode clock, outside the Hunters' Lodge, 855 pule. Last save: slot 1 at the Lanu's Grove totem, 1:11 save clock, 810 pule.

Stuck and confusing

1. Water for Lanu's posts (third episode running). The post says "A post for Lanu. I need a cup of water to leave her an offering." There is no cup item in any bag page. Faced the Crossroads lake and pressed z: "Just foam and sand." Faced the sparkling pond next to the post and pressed z: "The party drinks from the cool pond. Everyone is rested." The grove villager said "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning." The answer (booklet): scoop at a non-sparkling river or pond; the canteens are hidden. Fixed at the pond screen's river: "Kailo scoops up some fresh water."

2. The Sage, the quest giver, is not in Lanu's Grove. Walked every open part of the grove including the top rows. Quest text still says "go back and tell the sage".

3. North exit of the post screen north of the west maze: two Wild Boars stand in the gap behind a full row of palms. Walked the row below and pressed up at all twelve columns: the narrator's north-gap distance never changed.

4. The grove's east door drops into a sealed nook in the east forest. Pushed right at the palm column on both bottom rows (walk right 1, five times): no movement. The only way out is back west to the grove. The glade post is visible from it.

5. Four-chest screen: entering from the north puts you in a top pocket with the opened chest; the water and the other chests are behind palm rows.

6. Haste element: "KAILO can't learn this." and Hina's box greyed. No hint who can.

7. Miki's quest page says "You know now, so go to the hunters' lodge and tell her." Kailo has not met the brother. Talking to Miki: "Find my brother and tell me where he is. The bottle is yours."

8. Māla Iki: Miki says her brother "walked out of Māla Iki" and "I thought I'd left your kind behind on Māla Iki"; Gajumaru says Gin'imun "swam on... to Māla Iki". I had noted from the Loremaster that this island is Māla Iki.

9. The Bag Upgrade in the Trapper's list shows no price until you pick it (then Coir Belt, 300, per member).

10. Elemental hits still come with no parry meter ("Weak!" 48 on Hina from a light-stance Papanok; "Resisted" on Kailo).

11. Moving the cursor in the item list with right did nothing; L and R (q, e) flip the bag pages. Not shown on screen.

12. After a fight, the walk commands sometimes left Kailo a tile or two off from where I expected, which threw off maze routes (my bookkeeping, but the mazes have no landmarks to recover from).

Design notes

1. Praise: the turn bar preview changes as you move the cursor between Attack, Cook and Element. Every choice shows its cost in turns. Large.

2. Praise: parry strings are readable rhythm (Papanok's seven Lights) and a clean string earns a counter (28, 38). Large.

3. Praise: the Combo is a payoff the whole fight builds toward; Pōhuehue did 238. Large.

4. Problem: "a cup of water" sends the player looking for a cup. The post line should say fresh water from a river, or the first post should teach scooping. Two episodes lost. Large.

5. Praise with a caveat: light blue for fresh water and teal for salt on the area map is a good silent rule, but nothing teaches it. Small.

6. Problem: three sealed pockets in one session (north exit, four-chest top, east-door nook) that show you a goal you cannot reach. With no signpost it reads as teasing, not discovery. The hunter's axe line suggests a tool; say so sooner. Medium.

7. Problem: the quest giver for Lanu's posts has vanished, and the quest says to go back to him. Medium.

8. Bug: Miki's quest page says you know where her brother is before you do. Medium.

9. Praise: every piece of gear is a trade-off ("Spear. Strength up, Intelligence down."). Buying is a plan, not an upgrade. Medium.

10. Praise: the Hunters' Lodge hunt board turns story threats (Great Boar, the toll Nuno, a walking dead man) into bounties with prices, so the player gets a reason and a reward. Medium.

11. Praise: stats rise in the fight that trained them ("Kailo's Vitality up!", max HP 130 to 140 mid-fight). Small.

12. Praise: element descriptions show numbers ("12 physical fire, 20% burn."). Small.

13. Problem: elemental "Weak!"/"Resisted" blows still have no parry meter and no explanation. Medium.

14. Praise: Gajumaru's slow speech and his missed-boat line; the writing keeps being the best part. Small.

15. Problem: Hina's Heal is still about 18 at 170 max HP. Small.

16. Problem: Bag Upgrade shows no price in the list. Small.

Story and characters

The stew for Old Pono's wake is still the spine, and today it grew a second thread: Miki holds the shoyu and trades it for news of her brother. The world got wider. Gajumaru comes from the Kame Kingdom far to the northwest, carried by a Bandari trader from Kota Emas, so this is a whole ocean of cultures (Philippine spirits, Malay words, Okinawan ones, Hawaiian ones). The Hunters' Lodge put prices on the island's troubles: the Great Boar, the toll Nuno, six Aghoy, and a dead man who walks at night, on the night of a wake.

- Kailo: still one thing on his mind, the stew. Bargains for shoyu on the spot. I like that his first reaction to a stranger's family trouble is "Is that shoyu?"

- Hina: one sharp line today ("Funny. I was thinking the same about yours.") and a dig at shoyu. She's carrying more of the fights now; her Mediums hit 14 to 16.

- Miki: new. White hair, blunt, sister of a flake who walked out without a word; their mother keeps asking. Doesn't like Māla priestesses. Holds the last of her shoyu.

- Miki's brother: unmet. Tall, white hair, "a mouth that never stops", "looks like he's doing you a favor by existing".

- The Trapper: runs the Hunters' Lodge shop and hunt board. "E komo mai!"

- Gajumaru: a little tree spirit at the lodge table, speaks very slowly, plays Kaigara (Go), from the Kame Kingdom; his friend Gin'imun swam on to Māla Iki. Missed his boat mid-move.

- The Boy at the Inn: wants to show me his crab.

- The Sage: missing.

Predictions

- Right: the hunters' lodge exists and buys Boar Hide (50 each).

- Right: one of the walled east-side gaps was an entrance from an unexplored screen; the boar maze's west exit led to the lodge screen (a west gap, not east, but the same idea).

- Wrong: the island is Māla Iki. Miki and Gajumaru both speak of Māla Iki as somewhere else.

- Half right: "the fishing for the stew is Ama". The Boy says fish need a rod; who sells or gives the rod is still open.

- Open, new: the Walking Corpse is tied to Old Pono's wake and the Callers of Makua. I hope I'm wrong that it's Pono himself.

- Open, new: Haste belongs to a third party member (Melia, or whoever the Kagura Fan was for).

- Open, new: an axe is a Y tool that cuts the palm walls and opens the sealed pockets.

- Open, new: Miki's brother is someone Kailo will meet soon, and he talks a lot.

- Open, new: the Sage went to the Lost Woods, and the fifth post is there.

- Open: the island won't stay untouched past the opening.

- Open: Kailo will follow his dad or Hina off the island; boats are the way off (Kailo's father built the harbor's boats).

- Open: Old Pono's death and the Callers of Makua will connect.

- Open: the stew is the first real recipe, cooked at Noelani's fire.

- Open: the Great Boar is Lanu's, the boars take the taro because Lanu's share stopped being given, and watering all five posts wakes something.

- Open: the Kagura Fan was meant for someone else (it is also sold at the lodge for 200).

- Open: the south's "take Mana from a beaten champion" becomes a villain's idea.

- Open: the giant moth on the mountain is real and a boss.

- Open: Heal All belongs on Hina's second row.

- Right (earlier): the troll is a boss; Hina's flower side takes extra from fire; Hina is the priestess; the woods alone were too much.

- Wrong (earlier): Lanu's cups come from the Sage; the Life Totem revives in a fight; Hina has a revive; someone close to Kailo died (it was Old Pono; his dad left).

The booklet

Opened once, at about the 24 minute mark. Why: two episodes unable to water Lanu's posts; I had tried the Crossroads lake, the healing ponds, every person in the Inn and its shop, and the grove. What I looked for: "cup". Not in the booklet. Then "water": the "Fresh Water" section ("Face a river or a pond and press A to scoop up fresh water for cooking. Seawater is no good, and neither is the shore. A spring with little sparkles over it heals instead of giving water."). My eye also caught the fishing paragraph next to it (an Old Rod, tap Y to cast). It helped: the river on the pond screen worked. Where it disagrees with the game: the grove villager says "I bring Lanu water from the spring every morning", and the booklet says springs give no water. The booklet says nothing about cups, and the post never says "fresh water".

Review so far

Nuitai is a small, warm island RPG that wants every system to mean something in its world: you save by telling the gods what happened, you heal at Lanu's springs, your stances are your faiths, and the main quest is a stew for a funeral. The fights are the best thing in it. The chain of strokes, the turn bar that previews every choice, the parry rhythm and the Combo you build toward all click, and today they clicked every single fight. The writing is the other star: Hina, Gajumaru, a kid with a crab. Today the world opened up with the Hunters' Lodge, a hunt board and a real shop full of trade-offs.

What doesn't work is getting around and knowing what the game wants. Two episodes went to a "cup of water" that's really "scoop at a river". The palm mazes keep sealing me into pockets that show me exactly what I can't reach. The quest giver for the posts has vanished, and one quest page is ahead of its own story. None of it is broken design at the core; it's signposting. Would I recommend it today? Yes, to someone who likes old-school exploration and is patient with it, mostly for the combat and the writing. For anyone else I'd wait for a pass on the signposts.

The canteens don't show in the bag. At a post: "Offer Lanu a cup of water?" Yes. Fresh water: the river across the top of the pond screen (north of the village west screen, south of the lodge screen); the stream in the lodge screen's top-left pocket (reached from its west gap only); the four-chest screen's bottom left (not from the north pocket). On the area map, light blue is fresh, teal is salt.

Lanu's posts, 3 of 5: pond screen (done Ep 1), grove (done Ep 1), north of the west maze (done today). Glade post in the east forest: not watered, reachable from the south loop (bridge, boardwalk, beach), NOT from the grove's east door (sealed nook). Fifth post: unknown. The map, as I know it now. Top row: grove, east forest (nook on its west, glade, Maika's stall, four-boar ring). - Trapper (lodge): shop (gear, Bag Upgrade "Coir Belt" 300 per member, Smoke Bomb 120), buys loot (Boar Hide 50, Blue/Green Wing 60, elements 75). Hunts: Great Boar 800 (taken), the toll Nuno "at the river bend" 600 (taken), Six Aghoy (didn't ask), Walking Corpse 1200 ("They say a dead man walks at night"; said Not now). "No kapa for sale. Monsters carry it... Each one has a move drawn on it."

- Hunters: "A Seer's Shell tells you what a beast is made of, and how much fight it has left." "Everyone who fights carries three kinds of weapon, and each kind has its own Skill. Whatever weapon you hold decides which Skill you can use." "A tree was in my way out there. Too thick to get around. I wished I had an axe."

- Gajumaru (lodge table): plays Kaigara (Go: black and white shells, surround to capture, black first, this game since last spring). From Kami Kuku, the Kame Kingdom, far northwest, green islands, clear springs, great turtles, they heal with what the springs give. Came with a Bandari trader from Kota Emas; his friend Gin'imun swam on to Māla Iki; he missed the boat thinking about his move. Play him.

Rules I learned: L/R flip bag pages. Seer's Shell scans an enemy. Haste can't be learned by Kailo or Hina. Flambé learned by Kailo, but his grid has one row (Sauté, Wave Guard). Sauté: "12 physical fire, 20% burn", 1 mark. Burn stops a boar's heal and ticks for 19. Combo appears when both are at 7 mana and next to each other on the turn bar. Gear is all trade-offs; Ananá set is fire resist, nature weak; Pearl Anklet shadow resist, spirit weak. Nothing resists spirit, which is what the Nuno uses.

Theories: this island is not Māla Iki; Māla Iki is the next island, home of Hina's priests and Miki's brother. The Walking Corpse ties to Old Pono and the Callers. An axe will open the palm pockets. Haste is for a third member.

Next time: water the glade post (south loop), look for the fifth post and the Sage (Lost Woods?), get a fishing rod (Ama at the harbor?) for 4 Fish, find Miki's brother, play Gajumaru, then the Nuno with full HP, Wave Guard, a heal in Hina's bag, and a save first. Bring Seer's Shells (I have three or four) and use one on the Nuno.
